item.title: France hold nerve to edge past South Africa in thriller
item.description: France were magnificent in attack in the first half but did not score a point in the second [Getty Images] Nations Championship France (21) 21 Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang, Attissogbe, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Lucu (3) South Africa (7) 19 Tries: Wessels, Reinach, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2) France held on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris. The victory dents the world champions' hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts Les Bleus in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings. The hosts, inspired by their captain Antoine Dupont, showed their class and skill to score three first-half tries in an action-packed game. France's back three of Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed in a thrilling opening 40 minutes, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels scoring off the back of a maul for the visitors. The Springboks thought they had a second try on the stroke of half-time but Kurt-Lee Arendse's try was chalked off after he strayed marginally offside. Number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card early in the second half - the third of four cards shown the game - for a shoulder charge, but it had the opposite effect to derailing the world champions. With South Africa's set-piece power proving too much, replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcolm Marx scored to set up a thrilling finale. However, Manie Libbok missed the vital conversion to Marx's try that would have levelled the game. With South Africa pushing for a winning score, Bielle-Biarrey produced a huge defensive tackle to force the ball loose, before Dupont, who was named player of the match, gathered possession to help seal the victory. The result will come as a blow to both England and Ireland, who are in direct competition with France for a place in the Nations Championship final at the end of the month. Les Bleus, who are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings, now face Argentina next Saturday, putting them in a strong position to reach the inaugural final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November. It was an electric start from the hosts, as a clever move sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap, with Grandidier-Nkanang eventually crossing in the corner. item.title: Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings
item.description: France ended South Africa's 100% record in the Nations Championship with a sensational 21-19 victory over the world champions at the Stade de France on Friday. Les Bleus' fourth victory from five pool matches extended their lead in the northern hemisphere standings to six points with one game to play. South Africa remain top of the standings in the southern hemisphere but will be overtaken by New Zealand if the All Blacks beat Wales in Cardiff on Saturday. England will hope to close the gap to France when they face Japan at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Steve Borthwick's side are in second place on points difference in the northern pool after an emphatic 45-22 victory over Australia last weekend. Ireland secured a 42-12 win over Argentina and are third, with Fiji their visitors in Dublin on Saturday. Scotland, who lost to New Zealand last week, are in fourth place with two wins and two defeats and face Australia at Murrayfield on Sunday. Wales overcame Japan 28-21 in their first home match of the championship, but remain in fifth place. France will be favourites to secure their place in the inaugural final when they face Argentina in the last round of pool matches on 21 November. The finals weekend takes place from 27-29 November, with all six matches at Allianz Stadium and the title match bringing the championship to a conclusion. item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson Could Beat The Odds For Munich Game
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Rhamondre Stevenson is not staying on the sideline for long. The Patriots running back worked off to the side during a walkthrough in Germany on Thursday. This move signals a return much sooner than the initial knee injury reports suggested. Pats Pulpit noted his presence offers real optimism for Sunday’s matchup against the Detroit Lions. He is expected to miss a couple of weeks after the injury in Week 9. He suffered the issue late in the third quarter of the 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Reports say the knee tendon problem near the back of his knee did not need surgery. Yet the media got the timeline wrong, according to Drake Maye. “I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time,” Maye said. Teammates See The Grind The locker room knows Stevenson wants to be back on the field. He is trying to help the team win a big one before the bye week arrives. Maye described him as a great player who can help the squad right now. “This is a time for players, a lot of the players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with their teammates and knowing that he’s a great player and can help us out,” Maye added. Teammate DeMario Douglas sees the work ethic up close. He called Stevenson a dawg who refuses to quit. “I know some people that probably be like, ‘Man, I ain’t even going to try’, you but his situation, man, I be talking to him [and he’s] like, ‘I’m going to try. I’m going to do what I can do.’ He’s working, he’s getting better. So, when the time comes, I know he’s working to get better,” Douglas said. Reality Check For Fantasy Owners Optimism is high, but the medical reality remains tricky. According to RotoBaller, it would be quite shocking if Stevenson plays during Week 10. Fantasy managers must continue to anticipate that Stevenson will remain inactive this weekend. Should he fail to receive approval to play in Germany, Corey Kiner will replace him as New England’s primary back facing the Lions. The Patriots face the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET in Munich.

item.title: Dupont praises France late grind in South Africa victory
item.description: France captain Antoine Dupont was all over the pitch, according to his coach Fabien Galthie (Anne-Christine POUJOULAT) France captain Antoine Dupont said on Friday that beating Rugby World Cup holders South Africa 21-19 was important to show that his side are capable of grinding out victories when it matters. Dupont's outfit held off a stirring second-half Springbok comeback in Paris to remain top of the northern hemisphere table in the Nations Championship having come into the fixture as underdogs. The half-back, who turns 31 on Sunday, put in a player of the match performance as Les Bleus kept out the visitors with a last-gasp defensive effort, succeeding where they had failed in a World Cup quarter-final lost by a single point three years ago. "In the head it's important to win matches that count, that are tough, that go down to the last minute," Dupont told broadcaster TF1. "It shows the mentality of the team that never gave in, even if we had it hard on our line," the 2021 World Rugby player of the year added. Dupont was named to start the game at fly-half for a first time in international rugby with France down to their fifth-choice playmaker after Romain Ntamack's injury in last weekend's win over Fiji. Despite wearing the number 10 jersey, Toulouse's Dupont featured in his regular scrum-half position with Maxime Lucu in the nine shirt but deputising for Ntamack. Head coach Fabien Galthie paid tribute to his captain, joking that he had been all over the pitch playing in several positions. He even helped hold up South African flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit over the line to deny South Africa a try and won a crucial turnover to see out the game. "Sometimes I call him a good back rower, he doesn't like that much but he was a good back rower today," said Galthie. "He played at nine, a little bit of 10, and a good six. "And he kicked well. A six who can kick as well -- the complete package. "He doesn't want to play at hooker, but if you ask me, he played a bit in every position. item.title: Billy Horschel And Chris Kirk Face The Harsh Reality Of The FedEx Cup Cutoff
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The clock has run out on excuses for the players hovering near the bottom of the FedEx Cup standings. Just two tournaments remain for golfers to earn playing privileges for the 2027 season, and the margin for error is gone. The autumn swing is not a holiday; it is used to identify golfers who are not ready for the main stage. The Bubble Boys Are Real Max Greyserman sits at No. 97, holding his status by a thread after a rough 2026 campaign. He managed a T10 and a T11 finish in the fall to stay inside the magic number, but that is not enough to feel safe. Billy Horschel, an eight-time winner, has not recorded an individual top-10 finish this year. He sat out the summer of 2025 with an injury and has struggled to regain his old form. Horschel has four top-15 finishes since the Canadian Open, yet he missed the cut in Cabo. These next two venues should suit his style better, but the pressure is immense. Chris Kirk faces a different challenge as the No. 102 ranked player. Should any golfer shift from outside to inside across the next two competitions, Kirk stands as the top prospect. The consequences are evident: conditional status or a drop to lower tours awaits them unless they rediscover the game that secured their PGA Tour spot. Success Is Not Guaranteed Some players have already locked up their status for years to come. Austin Smotherman won two tournaments this fall and secured his spot through the 2029 season. Jacob Bridgeman and Michael Brennan also added to their season tallies, proving they belong. But the spotlight belongs to the losers right now, not the winners. For fortunate golfers holding status from past achievements yet lacking guarantees, autumn brings the suffering of the previous year. The Austin Championship and the RSM Classic will decide the fate of these players in the coming weeks. The 2027 season is just around the corner, and there is no time for a slow start. The top 125 in the FedEx Cup gets conditional status, which is a scary place to be for anyone who wants to make a living on tour. The field is deep, and the competition is fierce as the PGA Tour wraps up its season. Only the best will survive the final cut line. Only two events remain for competitors to secure playing rights for the 2027 campaign.

item.title: FAA ground stop does not affect Wisconsin football game vs Maryland
item.description: Wisconsin football has made it safely to Maryland as the FAA’s nationwide ground stop affects travel for many other Week 11 college football games. The Badgers ’ team charter flight took off from Madison’s Dane County Regional Airport at 1:58 p.m. CT and landed in Baltimore at 4:43 p.m. ET, per UW sports information. The FAA issued the ground stop on the afternoon of Nov. 13, citing an air traffic control issue that led to extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns . U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a tweet that it is a communication issue that impacts all air traffic control centers. Other Big Ten road teams were not as fortunate as the Badgers . Minnesota, Purdue and Washington have been affected, according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , ahead of their respective games against Penn State, Iowa and Michigan State. A Big Ten spokesman told Thamel that all of the league’s officials are on site and not affected by the FAA ground stop. item.title: Lynch: Remembering Dan Hicks | Opinion
item.description: A few years back, I sat next to Dan Hicks in an Orlando steakhouse talking about working in television, which he’d been doing to acclaim for decades and I, stutteringly, for a hot minute. I asked a question that I often put to accomplished companions at dinner: what was the worst screw-up from which he learned the most? He didn’t hesitate to search for an answer. Dan recalled one of his earliest assignments in golf for NBC Sports, at what was then known as the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic. He was emceeing the trophy presentation on the 18th green, during which he was to be alongside the tournament host, who even then was well stricken in years. Ahead of the ceremony, he received a final word of advice from Tommy Roy, the longtime NBC golf producer. “Do not, under any circumstances,” Roy told him, “lose the microphone.” Sitting in that restaurant years later, Hicks gave a comical account of a tug-of-war that went entirely unnoticed by viewers. As he welcomed in Hope, Dan hovered his stick mic closer to the legendary entertainer so that he might offer a few words. Hope attempted to take it. Dan held on. Almost imperceptibly, Hope tugged a little harder. Smile fixed, Dan kept a Vulcan death grip. In the end, he lost out to guile and experience when Hope snatched the mic and turned to address the crowd. Dan described hearing an anguished, guttural groan in his earpiece from the production truck. “Uggghhhhh.” What remained of the broadcast would now run on Bob Hope’s schedule, not Tommy Roy’s. That was the last time Dan lost control of the microphone, which he wielded with assurance and diligence until his unexpected passing on Nov. 11 at the age of 64. His was a career that seemed to have precious few screw-ups that might be rendered fodder for laughs over dinner, but he’d probably argue the over on that. A summer evening in St Andrews with Dan, 2022. We joked about being the only guys in the photo without a PGA Tour win. pic.twitter.com/919WqGzmzt — Eamon Lynch (@eamonlynch) November 12, 2026 For more than three decades, he was the soundtrack to some indelible memories for sports fans, whether they were following the exploits of Tiger Woods, Michael Phelps, or Notre Dame football. He knew exactly what to say and — just as importantly — when to say nothing at all. Some of his finest moments have been played on a loop in recent days, like the “Expect anything different?” call as Woods forced a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open, and the frantic closing seconds of the men’s swimming relay race at the Olympics that same summer. The blessing of having excelled in a high-profile job is that he leaves an admirable body of work through which he will be remembered. Others have memories that are more personal, but equally enduring. My relationship with Dan was one of casual friendship. item.title: Queta’s Rise And Historic Road Trip Prove Celtics Depth Is Real
item.description: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics just did something no one in franchise history has ever done. They swept a four-game road trip with a plus-86 point differential, the best mark the team has ever posted in such a span. This wasn’t just a lucky streak; it was a masterclass in resilience. The team erased a 22-point deficit to beat the Toronto Raptors 98-93 on Wednesday night, improving their record to 10-2 overall, according to New Hampshire Union Leader . Most teams would crumble after such a big hole. The Celtics did the opposite. They rallied to win their fifth straight game, showing a poise that goes beyond simple talent. Joe Mazzulla credited the whole group for the win. He noted that even the bench players who did not see court time provided a massive lift in energy. The Big Man Steps Up With Paul George out due to illness, the big man stepped into the starting role alongside Luka Garza. Queta finished with 11 points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks against the Raptors. He also showed an expanded shooting touch, hitting three 3-pointers this season, which is already a career high for him. Derrick White praised Queta’s growth and impact on both ends of the floor. Queta agreed that the team feeds off each other’s energy. He noted that many players made energy plays that galvanize teammates and that feeding off each other is something the team needs to do more to get over the hump most nights. Depth That Wins Games This win was a full-team effort, not just a star-driven display. Mitchell Robinson was seen cheering on his teammates during the postgame scrum, offering high praise to White and Queta after the big man sealed the game with two free throws. The locker room vibe stayed high even after a flight delay, with players like Payton Pritchard and Ron Harper Jr. running the DJ duties for the postgame jam session. The Celtics have now won 9 of their last 10 games, a stretch that includes a 7-1 run over eight games in 13 days. This depth and ability to win tight games show why they are playing 11 guys every night and leaning on such a deep roster to chase a title.

item.title: Philip Rivers’ introductory press conference set for Monday
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Former NC State quarterback Philip Rivers attends the game between the North Carolina Tar Heels and the NC State Wolfpack at Carter-Finley Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images NC State made it official today that Philip Rivers will be the football program’s next head coach, and he will be introduced on Monday afternoon at 1:30 p.m. ET. ACC Network will carry the press conference live. Rivers’ deal with NC State is reportedly worth $3.25 million annually over five seasons, and the buyout is his salary multiplied by the number of years remaining on his deal. This part of the risk, at least, is relatively inexpensive. From NC State’s press release : “I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University,” Rivers said. “In many ways, I feel like I’m coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. “I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. There’s no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we’re not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory.” Philip is one of the most competitive guys out there, and hopefully he can channel that in the right way in this new position, because it’s going to be a lot for him. As with all new coaching hires, I’ll be cautiously optimistic until proven otherwise.

item.title: Dodgers Legend Orel Hershiser Reveals Why LA Will Fight to Keep Tarik Skubal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers legend Orel Hershiser talked to Dodgers Nation in an exclusive interview about his outlook on Tarik Skubal’s free agency. As a key member of the Sportsnet LA broadcast and someone who has been around the team for decades, Hershiser knows what it takes to deliver when pitching at The Ravine. In his eyes, Skubal is the kind of guy who has more to show Dodgers fans , beyond his 2.61 ERA in his 10 appearances. Why he thinks the Dodgers will be aggressive to keep Skubal While Skubal was certainly good overall and great in stretches, he wasn’t the pitcher who won two straight Cy Young awards. Sep 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal celebrates after clinching the National League West title after the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images That guy, Hershiser says, is still there, and it will show whenever he pitches next. “I don’t think we’ve seen his best yet, and I think they will try as hard as they can to sign him because what we saw was a guy who fit into a team with amazing chemistry, and he fit right in,” Hershiser told Dodgers Nation. Beyond his fit, Hershiser, nicknamed the “Bulldog,” sees grit in Skubal that earned the Hall of Famer’s respect. “What we saw was a guy who couldn’t wait to take the ball. Even though he’s going to be a free agent, he would have come back on short rest,” Hershiser said. “He would have pitched multiple times. He would have pitched deeper into games than you normally would want him to, if you were thinking about the long term and his health.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) While not going as far as to predict Skubal would return, Herischier was not shy about noting that he is a player the Dodgers typically pursue aggressively. “I think we saw a very, very competitive guy, a very, very professional guy, a great student of the game, and a great teammate. And I think all of that increases his value, and the Dodgers would want him.” Oct 20, 1988; Oakland, CA, USA: FILE PHOTO; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Orel Hershiser reacts after defeating the Oakland Athletics in the 1988 World Series at Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum. Hershiser was named series MVP. Mandatory Credit: MPS-USA TODAY Sports The Skubal-Hershiser parallels Hershiser knows a thing or two about what it takes to be at the top of a rotation and carry the mantle of being a Cy Young Award winner. He and Skubal share that honor, along with the ability to claim they were the best pitcher alive for years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Hershiser was part of the Dodgers’ last golden era, during which the franchise won its last title since the 2020s. Looking ahead to 2027 and beyond, if he stays, Skubal could cement himself as the next feisty Dodgers ace to bring a title to Los Angeles — as Koufax, Kershaw, and even Hershiser did.

item.title: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack
item.description: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack Michael Carrick paid the ultimate price for Manchester United’s dismal start to the season, with the Red Devils languishing in 18th position in the Premier League after winning only once so far. The former head coach received his marching orders amid complaints about the squad’s poor fitness levels and tactical blunders. INEOS’ role in this whole fiasco cannot be taken lightly, as they failed to back the Englishman in the summer. Add to this key players underperforming, and such a scenario was bound to happen. One of last season’s top performers , goalkeeper Senne Lammens, has struggled to replicate that form , with the Belgian failing to keep a single clean sheet in the league. Lammens on INEOS’ call to sack Carrick He arguably had the worst game of his United career so far against Aston Villa, in what turned out to be Carrick’s final game in charge. The 24-year-old was asked about Carrick’s dismissal after his country’s international friendly against Türkiye. He explained that INEOS’ decision was a tough pill to swallow for the whole squad, which had shown through recent results that they were fully behind the former United midfielder. “Yes, these are difficult weeks. I’m not going to lie about that,” he admitted. “Of course, as a Manchester United team, we need to do better. Why United were forced to sack Carrick “Now the manager has been sacked. It’s obviously a difficult time, both for me and for the whole team. We were all behind him.” After the Bournemouth debacle, United’s co-owners had reportedly handed Carrick a three-game ultimatum . It started in disastrous fashion. The 20-time English league champions showed promise in the first half against Chelsea before Lisandro Martínez single-handedly dragged his team down. A trademark comeback in the Champions League against AS Roma followed, and despite a come-from-behind 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, INEOS decided to pull the plug. item.title: Joshua Kimmich insists he has “no problems” with his ankle after dangerous tackle
item.description: Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images Joshua Kimmich received a heavy tackle from substitute Vanja Dragojević in the 76th minute of Germany’s 3-1 UEFA Nations League victory against Serbia. Kimmich went down clutching his ankle leaving German — and especially Bayern — fans holding their breath. The German captain managed to finish the game. However, many remained concerned there could have been some damage to the midfielder’s joint. In a post-match interview, Kimmich eased worries. When asked whether the knock he took would be an issue ahead of Germany’s high-stakes clash against the Netherlands on Monday, Kimmich insisted he had “no problems” with his ankle. “No, there are no problems at all,” said the 31-year-old midfielder (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern Munich already have a laundry list of injuries. The last thing Die Rekordmeister needed was an injury to their midfield lynchpin. Thankfully, it appears Kimmich is healthy. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. item.title: Brajan Gruda on his dream debut goal for Germany
item.description: BELGRADE, SERBIA - NOVEMBER 13: Brajan Gruda of Germany celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Serbia and Germany at Rajko Mitic Stadium on November 13, 2026 in Belgrade, Serbia. (Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brajan Gruda is in dreamland. The 22-year-old German forward had his breakout a few seasons ago for Mainz — earning rave reviews from Bayern Munich and national team legend Thomas Müller at the time — but his career has taken a circuitous path since. His big move to England did not pay off, at least not quickly, and after a nondescript season-and-a-half at Brighton, Gruda found himself back in the Bundesliga, this time on loan at RB Leipzig. But this year, it is all starting to come together. New Germany boss Jürgen Klopp has been keen on incorporating the dynamic attacker’s skills into the men’s national team setup; Gruda narrowly missed a call-up in September due to injury to Klopp’s super-sized squad. But his season at Leipzig has been promising — two goals and five assists across all competitions. When Klopp trimmed the roster for his second international period, Gruda still made the cut. Now he is taking his break and running with it. Friday against Serbia in a quiet, rain-sodden Belgrade stadium (largely devoid of fans owing to a UEFA spectator ban for the match), Gruda earned a place in Klopp’s XI for his Germany debut. He left having terrorized the Serbian defenses with a man-of-the-match performance, and collecting a dazzling goal after dribbling halfway down the pitch. All while being the man to don the #10 shirt — which he is fitting very, very well in. “Jo [Kimmich] was on the ball, and with my first touch, I moved inside,” Gruda said of his higlight-reel moment (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “There was so much space that I thought I had to take advantage of it. And the fact that they weren’t closing me down was good for me too, so I simply made the most of it. It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling. I just do it. I don’t think there’s really time to think anyway. It just happens. That’s it.” Gruda’s effort put Germany up 3-0 after just 50 minutes, proving to be the dagger en route to a commanding 3-1 win . item.title: Kenneth Walker Injury Threatens Chiefs’ Rushing Momentum
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Kenneth Walker III, the running back for the Kansas City Chiefs, missed Friday practice because of a sore groin, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday’s game. The team lacks a top rusher after an injury created a gap in the lineup. In his first season with the squad, Walker has accumulated 872 rushing yards, trailing the league lead by just eight yards. His per-game average of 109 yards leads the entire NFL, so his absence would be a major blow if he cannot play. Reid Backs the Rookie Head coach Andy Reid knows the pressure is on, yet he remains calm about the backup plan. Reid stated that the team will monitor Walker’s condition leading into Sunday, but he is not panicking about the loss of production. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not,” Reid said regarding the game plan. The coach has total faith in the young players ready to step up if the starter cannot go. “Everybody has confidence in him,” Reid added when asked about the depth chart. Rookie Emmett Johnson is the name on everyone’s lips if Walker sits out. Johnson is a fifth-round pick out of Nebraska who has already shown he can handle big touches. He has rushed for 111 yards and a touchdown on just 26 carries this season. The rookie also secured 14 catches for 237 yards and another score, demonstrating he is a complete back. Should Walker be unable to play this weekend, Johnson stands ready to assume a larger workload. Other Keys to the Game The offense has other pieces moving into place for the trip to Atlanta. Wide receiver Josh Downs plans to participate days after being traded from Indianapolis. Just before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, the Chiefs acquired Downs from the Colts. Reid praised the new receiver’s quick learning curve, noting, “I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days.” Health concerns linger elsewhere, but the team expects wide receiver Xavier Worthy to be available after he left the previous game with a hamstring injury. The New Haven Register reports that the squad still lacks wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who sits on injured reserve because of a dislocated ankle. Reid called Downs a smart kid who knows how to play. The Chiefs face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET in Mercedes-Benz Stadium. According to the Associated Press, Walker has participated in one fewer game this year than the Atlanta Falcons running back, producing a distinctive statistic for the matchup. Walker has caught 22 balls for 172 yards and four touchdowns, showing his value as a receiver out of the backfield. The team will see how Walker’s sore groin holds up before making a final call on his status. “We’ll see. He’s not one to say something like that (without meaning it),” Reid said.

item.description: The final semifinal spot in the WTA Finals was on the line Friday afternoon as Aryna Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina matched wits in a winner-take-all clash at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. The winner's prize? A spot in Saturday's semifinals to play Linda Noskova. The loser would see her tournament come to an end. On this day it was the Ukrainian Svitolina showing unlimited resolve as she dispatched Sabalenka, the highest-ranked player in the field, with a gutsy 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 victory. After the final point and shaking the chair umpire's hand, Svitolina raised her arms in joy and stared skyward with the biggest smile she's worn in months. It's been a tumultuous time for Svitolina going through a public divorce on top of the ongoing war in her home country. War and peace: Ukrainian Elina Svitolina finds inspiration at WTA Finals Svitolina, the No. 6 seed who won this tournament in 2018, will move into the semifinals with Mirra Andreeva (3), Jessica Pegula (5) and Linda Noskova (8). Saturday's WTA Finals semifinals are all set as it will be Svitolina vs. Noskova and Pegula vs. Andreeva. Whether it will be there when the calendar turns to January is still very much up in the air. item.title: Jonathan Taylor Says Trade Talks Are Above His Pay Grade
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) waves to fans as he leaves the field Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after losing a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Despite intense speculation connecting them to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, the New York Giants made no moves by the NFL trade deadline. Per reports, while a second-round and a fifth-round pick were reportedly offered, the transaction failed to complete before the deadline arrived. As a 2-7 Indianapolis Colts member, Taylor stayed put and expressed his views clearly during his initial media session after the deadline expired. Taylor Takes The High Road Speaking with reporters, Taylor was blunt when asked about not getting traded to a contender like the Giants. He told the media that trade decisions are way above his pay grade and that he is glad he does not have to make those hard calls. Taylor stated that his only job is to come in and make sure he is at his best each and every single day for his coaches and teammates. He told reporters, according to Heavy.com , “I would hate to be in that situation. But I know that they have a vision and a plan for it.” While Giants fans might have wanted a blockbuster move, Taylor seems content to just execute the plan the Colts have set out for him right now. He emphasized that the best thing to help the team is executing and getting a win versus Miami. Why The Colts Held Firm It is easy to wonder why the Colts did not trade their best remaining player when they are sitting at 2-7 and have no first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. ESPN’s Dan Graziano stated that Indianapolis felt no urgency to trade since Taylor is signed through the 2028 season. The front office clearly decided that keeping their star running back was more valuable than the premium picks they could have gotten in return. Several weeks prior, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and on Tuesday they also parted ways with wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. Unlike other key departures, Taylor was not moved, and he never asked for a trade or stated a desire to leave. This silence suggests he is willing to ride it out in Indy while the team rebuilds around him. Giants Find Value Elsewhere The Giants missed out on the biggest name at the deadline, but they did not mortgage their future for an overpriced player. GM Joe Schoen stood pat because the asking prices for defensive tackles were too steep and the team only has five picks in the 2027 draft. Rather than exchanging picks, the organization noted that rookie defensive lineman Bobby Jamison-Travis has gained more playing time and recorded a 77.5 run‑defense grade versus the Texans, per reports.
